I've done a few section hikes on the AT. A week at a time and about 80-100 miles per week. It takes most of the week to get your legs right. My problem is pack weight. I always bring too much stuff and my pack sits around 80 pounds. In the future, I'm going to look into ultra lite packing. I've been camping a lot with just a hammock and tarp and want to incorporate just that.

There is a lot of information and help on some of the AT message boards. You can even hitch rides so that you can leave a car at your endpoint. It's been a while since I've used them but a simple search will bring most of them up.

When you hike, especially in the rough areas, it's nice to think about how you are somewhere that very few people have ever been.

80 pounds is pretty extreme, i was going to say i couldnt imagine it but then i looked at what i pack and i easily imagined reaching 80.

My tent is a tiny 1 person combat shelter, massively overweight for the size, but if i wanted an equally durable two person, or a "lightweight" 4 person dome, id easily triple that weight.

And the stool i have is two pounds, ultra light, but its on the kill list for me cutting weight, but ive taken a full size camp chair with me before, thats like ten times the weight.

And then food and water, oh god food and water. I currently think i have 20 pounds of food and water, 10 each, packed. And thats ONLY enough food to keep me alive and walking for a week, on a calorie deficit. And enough water to last maaaaybe 2 days before i have to find a source, filter it with my sawyer mini, boil the filtered water (i do NOT want to be pissing out of my ass while i hike), a few ounces at a time in my singular cooking/boiling pot, over a fire i have to start with a lighter and some fire starter or a fuel cube that should boil like 4 pots of water per cube ideally. I feel like I'm extra stressed over food and water, i don't like sipping puddles.

But yea, i can see carrying 80 if you want room, comfort, and plenty of good food and water.

Right now my base weight is roughly 30lbs, give or take 5 or 6 depending what i decide with a couple things. And my food and water is 20ish, so im starting my hike at roughly 50lbs spread through my rucksack and a couple smaller bags ive expertly strapped on for more space, and a small tactical waist pack (fanny pack) upfront for easy access items.

I'm trying to keep practicing with this loadout while i work on trimming it down to size, but i just cant bring myself to sacrifice some things. Like my tent. Milsurp combat tent, tough as hell, would save me from a small limb falling that would kill an ultralight tenter probably, fire and spark resistant so no burn holes from fire embers, blackout capable fly so i can sleep late or early if i want, vestibule for storing gear out of the rain but not in the tent, and it sets up FAST and EASY and doesnt require staking or tying for anything. I feel like that is totally worth the six pounds it costs me. Compared to spending $400 for a pair of yoga pants to climb into (thats my interpretation of every ultralight tent ive seen) just because they weigh 6oz. Ill take comfort and durability for 6lbs please.

I lay everything out before hand and start picking out stuff I don't need. Then I pack it up and realize that it still way too heavy.. So I start over. And still way too heavy. I always end up figuring out half the stuff I thought I needed, I could have left behind. I've left small things like an extra multi tool behind at shelters for someone else to claim just to shave a few ounces. All while being pissed at myself for throwing away good stuff.

Then comes the food and water. When doing a week hike, there's not much reason for a resupply so I pack a week's worth of food. I try to stick to mostly dehydrated stuff. And filler like instant potatoes and egg noodles. I save the water until I'm actually hiking and try to have at least a gallon. If you are on the AT, water sources are welled mapped and you can plan when you can stop to refill. On that, I wouldn't bother with boiling. Get some aqua-mira tablets for when you think you need more than just the filter. I bring water flavor packets for when the taste is too strong. I also have a hand pump water filter. I think it's REI brand. It's awesome. The only time I've ever used extra measures was when I had to use standing water. I once ran out of water in a dry area at the bottom of the last climb for the day. My camelback sprung a leak. I slowed way down and paced myself and drank about a gallon when I hit the shelter, but I made sure I had extra water the next day. Plus we do what we call "camel up" and drink as much as possible in the evening and in the morning before starting again. I use a pocket rocket for cooking and my brother in law uses a alcohol stove he made from a soda can. I think he carries less weight for cooking overall, but I get a better heat. I don't know if you've looked into stoves but there are tons of lightweight stuff out there. I think the more basic the better. There's less parts to break. I also prefer a fire for cooking but sometimes that isn't feasible.

I usually bring a tent. It's a small 1 person tent that I can throw up in a minute. Just enough room for me and my pack. I've rolled into camp after dark before and had to throw the tent up and throw some food in my belly and pass out. As far as yours being strong, I've slept through some storms where I wish I had a sturdy structure. But the weight is probably your trade-off for having something heavy duty. My next venture, I think I'm going to either get a hammock tent or go with the hammock I have and a tarp. I use 550 cord to support the tarp so that would give me decent protection from falling stuff.

A full camp chair? Holy fuck, I thought I was crazy with some of the stuff I carry. But yeah, 80 pounds is super easy to hit. I've even cut down to 1 extra set of clothes. But not socks. Have extras of those. Rainy hiking sucks. And extra shoes. Something comfy to wear around camp. My shoes come off right after my pack when I get to camp.

I hadn't thought to use a fanny pack but I do hang all sorts of stuff on the front of me. Especially my water bottles for easy reach. It helps balance the load some also. But I always have to set my pack down to get important stuff out so I might have to borrow that idea.

I only take the whole chair deal on short things, like 2 miles to camping. But in those cases ill also be carrying 2 long guns and a duffel of shooting stuff sometimes too. Sucks hiking with your hands full but hey, gotta do what ya gotta do.

I think ive got my extras fairly well cut down already, i actually still need to add some small stuff like moleskin and bandaids. I think my major issue is my love for heavy duty gear. I see lightweight gear and its either gonna cost so much i cant afford to hike, or its made of tissue paper, or both. I figure toughen up and grow stronger to carry my impressive load, the ladies love that.

I need to test the flow on my sawyer, but i dont want to get it wet and store it wet until its time to start using it. Im weird about things sometimes. I assume i can just backwash it and let it dry out and itll be fine and im just being an idiot.

I will probably get some water purification tablets, i keep sitting down and thinking about how many of my little pots of water i would have to boil every day, and im starting to want to get a bigger cook pot.
